slowing down, releasing, and renewing
connecting to inner stillness and clarity
cleansing your emotional body
letting go of self-sabotaging patterns
remembering and embodying your essence
connecting to yourself, nature, and like-minded souls in a non-judgmental space
After the morning workshop, a nourishing lunch will be offered in a magical creekside setting beneath the shade of oak and bay trees. Your afternoon includes a cedar enzyme footbath with guided walking and seated meditations, your choice of a massage or facial and time in our renowned Japanese garden.

item.description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 7/15/26
AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE
EXHIBIT DATES: July 27 – August 30, 2026
RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich; Learn about their art and celebrate the show. Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist. Refreshments will be served.
Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens. Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette. Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur. “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard. item.title: Preserve the Season: Stone Fruit — Sat Aug 1, 10:00 AM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
Part of our monthly Preserve the Season series, this hands-on workshop explores practical techniques for capturing the best of the harvest. Guided by Christina Connelly of Apple Blossom Acres, you’ll learn the fundamentals of home preservation while working with the freshest stone fruit available that week. In this workshop you’ll: * Learn the basics of home preservation and safe canning practices * Work with peak-season stone fruit selected for flavor and quality * Understand how fruit, sugar, acidity, and pectin work together in preserves * Make a seasonal jam, preserved fruit, and fruit-based beverage ingredient * Gain the confidence to continue preserving summer fruit at home You’ll leave with one jam, one preserved fruit and one preserved beverage and the skills to continue preserving the harvest at home.

item.description: Join us for a guided tour of the Occidental Arts & Ecology Center’s demonstration gardens and living landscapes. When: Tours start at 1pm every first and third Saturday of the month, April through October. Where: Tours start and end at the OAEC Nursery. 15290 Coleman Valley Rd, Occidental, CA 95465. Upper Driveway. Important Information: No registration required—just show up! Please use the second driveway and park in the upper lot near the greenhouses. The tour route includes steep hills and unpaved dirt and gravel paths. Sturdy shoes, a brimmed hat, and weather-appropriate layers are recommended. item.title: River Run + Cold Plunge (with Sauna!) — Sat Aug 1, 5:00 PM — The Floathouse Petaluma
item.description: Trade your Saturday afternoon for a tidal adventure on the Petaluma River. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this guided Downriver Run takes you six scenic miles through wide-open wetlands and peaceful river landscapes in easy-to-use Hobie pedal kayaks. From 3–5 pm, ride the outgoing tide from The Floathouse Petaluma to Lakeville Landing Marina, where the experience can continue with an optional discounted sauna + cold plunge session at Sundrop Sauna from 5–6:30 pm. Warm up in the sauna, cool down with a plunge, and relax riverside in the golden evening light. Want to make it a floating picnic party? Add a Bella Box from La Bella Charcuterie, with omnivore, vegetarian, and vegan options available. This is Sonoma County river culture at its finest: movement, nature, community, wellness, and good vibes — all in one unforgettable afternoon. It is usually attended by a vibrant & diverse bunch of welcoming and friendly people, some of whom have practiced Soul Motion® for years, while some ~ never before. Participants are invited to travel across all landscapes, not just their favorite one: dancing by oneself, in duet, in ensemble with several people and eventually the whole room, or witnessing in stillness the beauty of another’s or of everyone’s dance. Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens. item.title: Hindsight 2026 — Sat Aug 8, 1:00 PM — The California
item.description:
The eight playwrights from across the U.S. include local playwright Caitlin Strom-Martin, Arianna Rose, Rhea MacCallum, Alan Brooks, Robb Willoughby, Dan Morra, Maury Zeff and Steve Koppman. The plays cover topics such as identity, immigration, social inequity and the perils of social media, and include a memory play, satire, comedy and drama. Hindsight Festival plays are performed as staged readings by a talented group of local actors working with multiple directors. Since its first, virtual production in 2020, Hindsight has introduced more than 50 new playwrights from around the world to local audiences, earning a reputation for showcasing innovative, provocative and entertaining scripts. Books of winning Hindsight play scripts by year are available for sale on Amazon and at The California Theatre. Tickets: $17 Advance, $22 at the Door \(plus $2 card processing fee\) Doors open 12:00pm. Show at 1:00pm.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
